rules.rule_name: Provider Screening Batch Initiation
rules.rule_description: The provider screening batch process must initialize by gaining access to the Provider Master File and the Screening Output File before any provider records can be read or screening results written.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Provider Screening Initiation
Open Provider Master File
Open Screening Output File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The PRVSCR01 provider screening batch program is invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Provider Master File must be opened for both reading and updating, and the Screening Output File must be opened for writing, so that provider records can be retrieved and screening results can be recorded

rules.rule_name: Sequential Provider Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: The program must read provider records one at a time from the Provider Master File in sequential order to ensure every provider record is evaluated for screening eligibility.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Pending Provider Selection
Read Next Provider Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Provider Master File has been successfully opened and the screening loop is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The program advances to the next iteration of the screening loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next sequential provider record is read from the Provider Master File; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is detected and the screening loop terminates

rules.rule_name: Unscreened Provider Filter
rules.rule_description: Only providers whose screening status is marked as UNSCREENED are eligible for the screening process. Providers already marked as screened (pass or fail) must be skipped to avoid duplicate screening.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Provider Status
= Unscreened?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the provider's current screening status
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the provider status is UNSCREENED, the provider is forwarded for screening checks; if the provider status is anything other than UNSCREENED (already screened), the record is skipped and the next provider record is read

rules.rule_name: Medicare Reciprocity Flag Evaluation
rules.rule_description: Before performing individual screening checks, the program must evaluate whether the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active. If active, the program relies on prior Medicare/PECOS screening results instead of performing independent checks. This flag has not been active since 2014, making this path effectively dead code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Medicare Reciprocity
Flag Active?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unscreened provider record has been selected for screening
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the Medicare Reciprocity system flag
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active, the program invokes the Medicare Reciprocity Check routine and auto-passes all four screening checks (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF); if the flag is inactive (the normal operational path), the program proceeds to perform each individual screening check independently

rules.rule_name: Medicare/PECOS Reciprocity Auto-Pass Override
rules.rule_description: When the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active, the program accepts prior Medicare/PECOS screening results as sufficient, automatically passing all four individual screening checks (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF) without performing independent verification. The output record is tagged as a PECOS-sourced screening record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Medicare Reciprocity Check
DEAD CODE - Never Executed
Query PECOS - Accept Medicare
Prior Screening Results
Auto-Pass All 4 Checks

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has been selected and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The Medicare Reciprocity Check routine is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: All four screening check results — License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File — are automatically set to PASS; the screening output record is tagged as a PECOS record; no independent verification queries are performed for this provider

rules.rule_name: State License Verification
rules.rule_description: Each unscreened provider must have their state license verified against the State Licensing Board to confirm they hold a valid and active license. The result of this check is recorded in the Screening Output File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:State License Verification
Query State Licensing Board
Verify Valid Active License

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has been selected for screening and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
acceptance_criteria.When: The License Check routine is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The provider's license status is verified; the License check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the License check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

rules.rule_name: OIG LEIE Exclusion Verification
rules.rule_description: Each unscreened provider must be checked against the OIG List of Excluded Individuals and Entities (LEIE) database to confirm the provider has not been excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs. The result is recorded in the Screening Output File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:OIG LEIE Exclusion Check
Query OIG LEIE Database
Verify Provider Not Excluded

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has passed the License check step and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
acceptance_criteria.When: The LEIE Exclusion Check routine is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The provider's exclusion status is verified against the OIG LEIE database; the LEIE check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the LEIE check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

rules.rule_name: SAM Debarment Verification
rules.rule_description: Each unscreened provider must be checked against the System for Award Management (SAM) debarment list to confirm the provider has not been debarred from receiving federal funds. The result is recorded in the Screening Output File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:SAM Debarment Check
Query System for Award Management
Verify Provider Not Debarred

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has passed the LEIE check step and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
acceptance_criteria.When: The SAM Debarment Check routine is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The provider's debarment status is verified against the SAM database; the SAM check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the SAM check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

rules.rule_name: SSA Death Master File Verification
rules.rule_description: Each unscreened provider must be checked against the Social Security Administration Death Master File (DMF) to confirm the provider is not deceased. The result is recorded in the Screening Output File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:SSA Death Master File Check
Query SSA Death Master File
Verify Provider Not Deceased

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has passed the SAM check step and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
acceptance_criteria.When: The SSA Death Master File Check routine is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The provider's vital status is verified against the SSA Death Master File; the DMF check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the DMF check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

rules.rule_name: Overall Screening Verdict Determination
rules.rule_description: After all four individual screening checks are completed, the program determines the overall screening verdict for the provider. A provider passes only if all four checks — License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File — return a passing result. Failure of any single check results in an overall screening failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Screening Verdict Determination
All 4 Checks Passed?
License + LEIE + SAM + DMF

acceptance_criteria.Given: All four screening checks (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF) have been completed for an unscreened provider
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the combined results of all four checks
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the License check result AND the LEIE check result AND the SAM check result AND the DMF check result are all PASS, the provider is marked as SCREENING PASSED; if any one or more of the four check results is not PASS, the provider is marked as SCREENING FAILED and the screening failure counter is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Provider Master Record Screening Verdict Update
rules.rule_description: After the screening verdict (pass or fail) has been determined, the provider's record in the Provider Master File must be updated to reflect the new screening status, ensuring the provider is no longer treated as unscreened in future runs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Provider Record Update
Write Updated Screening Verdict
Back to Provider Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A screening verdict of either SCREENING PASSED or SCREENING FAILED has been determined for the provider
acceptance_criteria.When: The program completes the verdict determination step
acceptance_criteria.Then: The provider's record in the Provider Master File is updated (rewritten) with the new screening verdict status — either SCREEN PASS or SCREEN FAIL — so that the provider will not be reprocessed as unscreened in subsequent batch runs

rules.rule_name: Screening Failure Summary Reporting
rules.rule_description: At the conclusion of the batch screening run, the program must report the total number of providers who failed screening, providing an operational summary for business users to review screening outcomes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:Screening Summary Reporting
Display Total Count of
Providers Who Failed Screening

acceptance_criteria.Given: All provider records in the Provider Master File have been processed and the end-of-file condition has been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The screening batch loop terminates
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the total count of providers who received a SCREENING FAILED verdict during the current batch run, identified under the program name PRVSCR01, before the program terminates

acceptance_criteria.Then: The program is identified as PRVSCR01 and this identifier is recorded as the active batch program for the screening run

rules.rule_name: Open Provider Master File for Read and Update Access
rules.rule_description: The Provider Master File must be opened with both read and update access at the start of the screening batch, so that provider records can be retrieved for screening and subsequently updated with screening outcomes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Provider Master File for Read and Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The provider screening batch program PRVSCR01 has been identified and is starting
acceptance_criteria.When: The batch process initializes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Provider Master File is opened with simultaneous read and update access, enabling the program to both retrieve provider records for screening and write back the screening results (Pass or Fail) to the same file

rules.rule_name: Open Screening Output File for Writing Results
rules.rule_description: A dedicated Screening Output File must be opened exclusively for writing at the start of the batch, so that individual screening check results for each provider can be recorded during the batch run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Screening Output File for Writing Results

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Provider Master File has been successfully opened for read and update access
acceptance_criteria.When: The batch process continues its initialization
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Screening Output File is opened in write-only mode, ready to receive individual screening check result rows (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF) for each provider processed during the batch

rules.rule_name: Initialize End-of-File Indicator Before Processing Begins
rules.rule_description: Before any provider records are read or screened, the end-of-file indicator must be set to indicate that processing has not yet reached the end of the Provider Master File, ensuring the batch loop processes all pending providers.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Initialize Processing Set End-of-File Flag to No

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the Provider Master File and the Screening Output File have been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The batch process completes its initialization phase
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end-of-file indicator is set to 'No' (not yet reached end of file), signaling that provider record retrieval and screening should begin and continue until all records have been evaluated

rules.rule_name: Continuously Process All Pending Providers Until File is Exhausted
rules.rule_description: Once initialization is complete, the batch must repeatedly select and screen providers from the Provider Master File, continuing this cycle until every record in the file has been evaluated and the end of the file is reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Pending Provider Selection

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Provider Master File and Screening Output File are open, and the end-of-file indicator is set to 'No'
acceptance_criteria.When: The batch process transitions from initialization to active processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program enters a continuous loop that selects the next provider record and performs screening for each, repeating this cycle until the end-of-file indicator is set to 'Yes' (all records in the Provider Master File have been read and evaluated)

rules.rule_name: Sequential Read of Provider Records from Provider Master File
rules.rule_description: The system reads provider records one at a time in sequential order from the Provider Master File to evaluate each provider for screening eligibility.

from Provider Master File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Provider Master File is open and available for sequential reading, and the end-of-file condition has not yet been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The system requests the next provider record from the Provider Master File in sequential order
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next available provider record is retrieved from the Provider Master File and made available for status evaluation, and the file read status is captured for end-of-file detection

rules.rule_name: End of File Detection to Terminate Provider Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: After each sequential read of the Provider Master File, the system checks whether all provider records have been processed. If the end of file is reached, the screening loop is terminated and no further providers are processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End of File
Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Provider Master File and the file read status has been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The file read status indicates that the end of the Provider Master File has been reached (no more records available)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end-of-file flag is set to TRUE, the provider processing loop is terminated, and the program proceeds to close files and report final results

rules.rule_name: Identify Providers with Unscreened Status for Processing
rules.rule_description: Each provider record retrieved from the Provider Master File is evaluated to determine whether the provider has an 'Unscreened' status. Only providers with this specific status are eligible to proceed through the screening workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Provider Status
= Unscreened?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been successfully read from the Provider Master File and the end-of-file condition has not been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the provider's current screening status field in the provider master record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the provider's status is 'Unscreened', the provider is forwarded to the screening process; if the provider's status is anything other than 'Unscreened' (e.g., already screened as pass or fail), the provider record is skipped with no action taken

rules.rule_name: Forward Unscreened Provider to Screening Process
rules.rule_description: A provider record identified as having an 'Unscreened' status is forwarded to the full screening process, which includes Medicare reciprocity check (if applicable), license verification, LEIE exclusion check, SAM debarment check, and SSA Death Master File check.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Process

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and the provider's screening status is confirmed as 'Unscreened'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the provider requires screening
acceptance_criteria.Then: The provider record is passed to the screening process (SCREEN-ONE-PROVIDER) where all applicable screening checks will be performed and the provider's master record will be updated with the screening outcome

rules.rule_name: Skip Provider Records That Are Already Screened
rules.rule_description: Provider records that do not carry an 'Unscreened' status are bypassed entirely. No screening checks are performed, no output records are written, and the provider's master record is not updated. The system moves on to read the next provider record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

No Action Required

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and the end-of-file condition has not been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The provider's screening status is NOT 'Unscreened' (i.e., the provider has already been screened as pass or fail, or holds any other non-unscreened status)
acceptance_criteria.Then: No screening action is taken for that provider record, no output is written for that provider, the provider's master record remains unchanged, and the system immediately proceeds to read the next provider record from the Provider Master File

rules.rule_name: Continue Processing Until All Provider Records Are Exhausted
rules.rule_description: The provider screening loop continues to read and evaluate provider records sequentially until every record in the Provider Master File has been read. Once the end of file is reached, the process is considered complete and the total count of screening failures is reported.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: All Providers Processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The provider screening loop is actively reading provider records from the Provider Master File
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected on the Provider Master File, indicating no more provider records remain to be processed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screening loop terminates, the Provider Master File and Screen Output File are closed, and the total number of providers that failed screening is displayed as the final program output

rules.rule_name: Medicare Reciprocity Flag Evaluation
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the Medicare Reciprocity feature is active before invoking the PECOS-based auto-pass logic. This flag has never been set to active since 2014, making the entire reciprocity branch permanently unreachable dead code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Medicare Reciprocity Flag Enabled?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider record has been identified as UNSCREENED and is being processed for screening
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the Medicare Reciprocity Flag (WS-RECIPROCITY-ON) to determine if PECOS-based screening should be applied
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED, the system proceeds to apply PECOS-based auto-pass screening for all four checks; If the Medicare Reciprocity Flag is DISABLED (which is always the case as the flag has never been activated since 2014), the system bypasses the entire Medicare Reciprocity Check and returns directly to the standard individual provider screening flow

rules.rule_name: PECOS Prior Screening Acknowledgement Log
rules.rule_description: When Medicare Reciprocity is enabled, the system logs a notification indicating that it is relying on Medicare/PECOS prior screening results rather than performing independent verification. This is dead code that has never executed since 2014.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log: Relying on Medicare PECOS Prior Screening Results

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag has been evaluated and found to be ENABLED (a condition that has never occurred since 2014)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system enters the Medicare Reciprocity Check processing branch
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system logs and displays the message 'PRVSCR01: RELYING ON MEDICARE/PECOS SCREENING' to indicate that Medicare's prior screening results are being accepted in lieu of independent checks

rules.rule_name: PECOS-Sourced Screening Record Tagging
rules.rule_description: When Medicare Reciprocity is active, the screening output record for the provider is tagged as PECOS-sourced, identifying that the screening result originates from Medicare's enrollment system rather than independent verification. This is dead code that has never executed since 2014.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Record as PECOS-Sourced Screening

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED and the system has logged reliance on PECOS screening results
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screening output record for the provider
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screening output record is marked with the PECOS source indicator (SCR-PECOS flag set to TRUE), identifying that this provider's screening result is derived from Medicare/PECOS enrollment data rather than independent checks

rules.rule_name: Medicare Reciprocity Auto-Pass All Four Screening Checks
rules.rule_description: When Medicare Reciprocity is enabled, all four mandatory screening checks — License verification, OIG LEIE exclusion, SAM debarment, and SSA Death Master File — are automatically set to PASS without performing independent verification, on the basis that Medicare/PECOS has already completed equivalent screening. This is dead code that has never executed since 2014.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Auto-Pass All 4 Checks: License = PASS, OIG LEIE = PASS, SAM = PASS, SSA DMF = PASS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED and the provider's screening output record has been tagged as PECOS-sourced
acceptance_criteria.When: The system applies the Medicare reciprocity auto-pass rule to the provider
acceptance_criteria.Then: All four screening check results are automatically set to PASS: License Check Result = PASS, OIG LEIE Exclusion Check Result = PASS, SAM Debarment Check Result = PASS, SSA Death Master File Check Result = PASS — without executing any independent verification against those four data sources

rules.rule_name: Avoidance of Duplicate Screening Under 42 CFR 455.410
rules.rule_description: The Medicare Reciprocity feature is designed to comply with 42 CFR 455.410, which permits Medicaid agencies to rely on Medicare's provider screening results to avoid duplicating screening work already performed by Medicare/PECOS. This policy-based bypass has been inactive since 2014 as the enabling flag was never activated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Avoids Duplicate Screening Work Per 42 CFR 455.410

acceptance_criteria.Given: A provider is enrolled in Medicare and has already been screened through the Medicare/PECOS enrollment system
acceptance_criteria.When: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED and all four screening checks have been auto-set to PASS based on PECOS results
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system accepts Medicare's prior screening as sufficient under 42 CFR 455.410, bypasses independent re-verification of License, OIG LEIE, SAM, and SSA DMF, and proceeds to the overall pass/fail determination using the four auto-passed results — thereby avoiding duplicate screening effort

acceptance_criteria.When: The provider is marked as SCREEN FAIL
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screening failure counter is incremented by 1, reflecting this provider as a failed screening case in the batch total

rules.rule_name: Screening Failure Summary Display at End of Batch
rules.rule_description: After all providers in the Provider Master File have been processed, the system displays the total number of providers who failed screening, providing an operational summary of the completed batch screening run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: All provider records in the Provider Master File have been read and evaluated for screening
acceptance_criteria.When: The end of the Provider Master File is reached and the batch processing loop completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays a screening failure summary message identified with program name 'PRVSCR01', showing the label 'SCREENING FAILURES=' followed by the final accumulated count of providers who failed screening during the batch run

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The PRVSCR01 provider screening batch program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Provider Master File must be opened for both reading and updating, and the Screening Output File must be opened for writing, so that provider records can be retrieved and screening results can be recorded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider Screening Batch Initiation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The provider screening batch process must initialize by gaining access to the Provider Master File and the Screening Output File before any provider records can be read or screening results written.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Provider Master File has been successfully opened and the screening loop is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program advances to the next iteration of the screening loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next sequential provider record is read from the Provider Master File; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is detected and the screening loop terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Provider Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must read provider records one at a time from the Provider Master File in sequential order to ensure every provider record is evaluated for screening eligibility.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the provider's current screening status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the provider status is UNSCREENED, the provider is forwarded for screening checks; if the provider status is anything other than UNSCREENED (already screened), the record is skipped and the next provider record is read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unscreened Provider Filter
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only providers whose screening status is marked as UNSCREENED are eligible for the screening process. Providers already marked as screened (pass or fail) must be skipped to avoid duplicate screening.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider record has been selected for screening
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the Medicare Reciprocity system flag
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active, the program invokes the Medicare Reciprocity Check routine and auto-passes all four screening checks (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF); if the flag is inactive (the normal operational path), the program proceeds to perform each individual screening check independently

all_rules.Rule_Name: Medicare Reciprocity Flag Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing individual screening checks, the program must evaluate whether the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active. If active, the program relies on prior Medicare/PECOS screening results instead of performing independent checks. This flag has not been active since 2014, making this path effectively dead code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has been selected and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Medicare Reciprocity Check routine is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All four screening check results — License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File — are automatically set to PASS; the screening output record is tagged as a PECOS record; no independent verification queries are performed for this provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: Medicare/PECOS Reciprocity Auto-Pass Override
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Medicare Reciprocity flag is active, the program accepts prior Medicare/PECOS screening results as sufficient, automatically passing all four individual screening checks (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF) without performing independent verification. The output record is tagged as a PECOS-sourced screening record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has been selected for screening and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The License Check routine is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's license status is verified; the License check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the License check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

all_rules.Rule_Name: State License Verification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each unscreened provider must have their state license verified against the State Licensing Board to confirm they hold a valid and active license. The result of this check is recorded in the Screening Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has passed the License check step and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The LEIE Exclusion Check routine is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's exclusion status is verified against the OIG LEIE database; the LEIE check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the LEIE check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

all_rules.Rule_Name: OIG LEIE Exclusion Verification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each unscreened provider must be checked against the OIG List of Excluded Individuals and Entities (LEIE) database to confirm the provider has not been excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs. The result is recorded in the Screening Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has passed the LEIE check step and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SAM Debarment Check routine is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's debarment status is verified against the SAM database; the SAM check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the SAM check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

all_rules.Rule_Name: SAM Debarment Verification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each unscreened provider must be checked against the System for Award Management (SAM) debarment list to confirm the provider has not been debarred from receiving federal funds. The result is recorded in the Screening Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has passed the SAM check step and the Medicare Reciprocity flag is inactive
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SSA Death Master File Check routine is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's vital status is verified against the SSA Death Master File; the DMF check result is set to PASS; the provider's NPI and the DMF check result are written as a row to the Screening Output File

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSA Death Master File Verification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each unscreened provider must be checked against the Social Security Administration Death Master File (DMF) to confirm the provider is not deceased. The result is recorded in the Screening Output File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All four screening checks (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF) have been completed for an unscreened provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the combined results of all four checks
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the License check result AND the LEIE check result AND the SAM check result AND the DMF check result are all PASS, the provider is marked as SCREENING PASSED; if any one or more of the four check results is not PASS, the provider is marked as SCREENING FAILED and the screening failure counter is incremented by 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Overall Screening Verdict Determination
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all four individual screening checks are completed, the program determines the overall screening verdict for the provider. A provider passes only if all four checks — License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File — return a passing result. Failure of any single check results in an overall screening failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A screening verdict of either SCREENING PASSED or SCREENING FAILED has been determined for the provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes the verdict determination step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's record in the Provider Master File is updated (rewritten) with the new screening verdict status — either SCREEN PASS or SCREEN FAIL — so that the provider will not be reprocessed as unscreened in subsequent batch runs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider Master Record Screening Verdict Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the screening verdict (pass or fail) has been determined, the provider's record in the Provider Master File must be updated to reflect the new screening status, ensuring the provider is no longer treated as unscreened in future runs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All provider records in the Provider Master File have been processed and the end-of-file condition has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screening batch loop terminates
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the total count of providers who received a SCREENING FAILED verdict during the current batch run, identified under the program name PRVSCR01, before the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screening Failure Summary Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the conclusion of the batch screening run, the program must report the total number of providers who failed screening, providing an operational summary for business users to review screening outcomes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The provider screening batch process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program is identified as PRVSCR01 and this identifier is recorded as the active batch program for the screening run

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Provider Screening Batch Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: The provider screening batch process is identified and registered under the program name PRVSCR01, establishing the context for all subsequent screening activities performed during this batch run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The provider screening batch program PRVSCR01 has been identified and is starting
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch process initializes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Provider Master File is opened with simultaneous read and update access, enabling the program to both retrieve provider records for screening and write back the screening results (Pass or Fail) to the same file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Provider Master File for Read and Update Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Provider Master File must be opened with both read and update access at the start of the screening batch, so that provider records can be retrieved for screening and subsequently updated with screening outcomes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Provider Master File has been successfully opened for read and update access
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch process continues its initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Screening Output File is opened in write-only mode, ready to receive individual screening check result rows (License, LEIE, SAM, DMF) for each provider processed during the batch

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Screening Output File for Writing Results
all_rules.Rule_Description: A dedicated Screening Output File must be opened exclusively for writing at the start of the batch, so that individual screening check results for each provider can be recorded during the batch run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Provider Master File and the Screening Output File have been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch process completes its initialization phase
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-file indicator is set to 'No' (not yet reached end of file), signaling that provider record retrieval and screening should begin and continue until all records have been evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize End-of-File Indicator Before Processing Begins
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any provider records are read or screened, the end-of-file indicator must be set to indicate that processing has not yet reached the end of the Provider Master File, ensuring the batch loop processes all pending providers.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Provider Master File and Screening Output File are open, and the end-of-file indicator is set to 'No'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch process transitions from initialization to active processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program enters a continuous loop that selects the next provider record and performs screening for each, repeating this cycle until the end-of-file indicator is set to 'Yes' (all records in the Provider Master File have been read and evaluated)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continuously Process All Pending Providers Until File is Exhausted
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once initialization is complete, the batch must repeatedly select and screen providers from the Provider Master File, continuing this cycle until every record in the file has been evaluated and the end of the file is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Provider Master File is open and available for sequential reading, and the end-of-file condition has not yet been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the next provider record from the Provider Master File in sequential order
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next available provider record is retrieved from the Provider Master File and made available for status evaluation, and the file read status is captured for end-of-file detection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Read of Provider Records from Provider Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads provider records one at a time in sequential order from the Provider Master File to evaluate each provider for screening eligibility.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Provider Master File and the file read status has been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file read status indicates that the end of the Provider Master File has been reached (no more records available)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-file flag is set to TRUE, the provider processing loop is terminated, and the program proceeds to close files and report final results

all_rules.Rule_Name: End of File Detection to Terminate Provider Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each sequential read of the Provider Master File, the system checks whether all provider records have been processed. If the end of file is reached, the screening loop is terminated and no further providers are processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been successfully read from the Provider Master File and the end-of-file condition has not been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the provider's current screening status field in the provider master record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the provider's status is 'Unscreened', the provider is forwarded to the screening process; if the provider's status is anything other than 'Unscreened' (e.g., already screened as pass or fail), the provider record is skipped with no action taken

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Providers with Unscreened Status for Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each provider record retrieved from the Provider Master File is evaluated to determine whether the provider has an 'Unscreened' status. Only providers with this specific status are eligible to proceed through the screening workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and the provider's screening status is confirmed as 'Unscreened'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the provider requires screening
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider record is passed to the screening process (SCREEN-ONE-PROVIDER) where all applicable screening checks will be performed and the provider's master record will be updated with the screening outcome

all_rules.Rule_Name: Forward Unscreened Provider to Screening Process
all_rules.Rule_Description: A provider record identified as having an 'Unscreened' status is forwarded to the full screening process, which includes Medicare reciprocity check (if applicable), license verification, LEIE exclusion check, SAM debarment check, and SSA Death Master File check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been read from the Provider Master File and the end-of-file condition has not been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider's screening status is NOT 'Unscreened' (i.e., the provider has already been screened as pass or fail, or holds any other non-unscreened status)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No screening action is taken for that provider record, no output is written for that provider, the provider's master record remains unchanged, and the system immediately proceeds to read the next provider record from the Provider Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Provider Records That Are Already Screened
all_rules.Rule_Description: Provider records that do not carry an 'Unscreened' status are bypassed entirely. No screening checks are performed, no output records are written, and the provider's master record is not updated. The system moves on to read the next provider record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The provider screening loop is actively reading provider records from the Provider Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected on the Provider Master File, indicating no more provider records remain to be processed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screening loop terminates, the Provider Master File and Screen Output File are closed, and the total number of providers that failed screening is displayed as the final program output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing Until All Provider Records Are Exhausted
all_rules.Rule_Description: The provider screening loop continues to read and evaluate provider records sequentially until every record in the Provider Master File has been read. Once the end of file is reached, the process is considered complete and the total count of screening failures is reported.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been identified as UNSCREENED and is being processed for screening
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the Medicare Reciprocity Flag (WS-RECIPROCITY-ON) to determine if PECOS-based screening should be applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED, the system proceeds to apply PECOS-based auto-pass screening for all four checks; If the Medicare Reciprocity Flag is DISABLED (which is always the case as the flag has never been activated since 2014), the system bypasses the entire Medicare Reciprocity Check and returns directly to the standard individual provider screening flow

all_rules.Rule_Name: Medicare Reciprocity Flag Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the Medicare Reciprocity feature is active before invoking the PECOS-based auto-pass logic. This flag has never been set to active since 2014, making the entire reciprocity branch permanently unreachable dead code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag has been evaluated and found to be ENABLED (a condition that has never occurred since 2014)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system enters the Medicare Reciprocity Check processing branch
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs and displays the message 'PRVSCR01: RELYING ON MEDICARE/PECOS SCREENING' to indicate that Medicare's prior screening results are being accepted in lieu of independent checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: PECOS Prior Screening Acknowledgement Log
all_rules.Rule_Description: When Medicare Reciprocity is enabled, the system logs a notification indicating that it is relying on Medicare/PECOS prior screening results rather than performing independent verification. This is dead code that has never executed since 2014.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED and the system has logged reliance on PECOS screening results
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screening output record for the provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screening output record is marked with the PECOS source indicator (SCR-PECOS flag set to TRUE), identifying that this provider's screening result is derived from Medicare/PECOS enrollment data rather than independent checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: PECOS-Sourced Screening Record Tagging
all_rules.Rule_Description: When Medicare Reciprocity is active, the screening output record for the provider is tagged as PECOS-sourced, identifying that the screening result originates from Medicare's enrollment system rather than independent verification. This is dead code that has never executed since 2014.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED and the provider's screening output record has been tagged as PECOS-sourced
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system applies the Medicare reciprocity auto-pass rule to the provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All four screening check results are automatically set to PASS: License Check Result = PASS, OIG LEIE Exclusion Check Result = PASS, SAM Debarment Check Result = PASS, SSA Death Master File Check Result = PASS — without executing any independent verification against those four data sources

all_rules.Rule_Name: Medicare Reciprocity Auto-Pass All Four Screening Checks
all_rules.Rule_Description: When Medicare Reciprocity is enabled, all four mandatory screening checks — License verification, OIG LEIE exclusion, SAM debarment, and SSA Death Master File — are automatically set to PASS without performing independent verification, on the basis that Medicare/PECOS has already completed equivalent screening. This is dead code that has never executed since 2014.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider is enrolled in Medicare and has already been screened through the Medicare/PECOS enrollment system
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Medicare Reciprocity Flag is ENABLED and all four screening checks have been auto-set to PASS based on PECOS results
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system accepts Medicare's prior screening as sufficient under 42 CFR 455.410, bypasses independent re-verification of License, OIG LEIE, SAM, and SSA DMF, and proceeds to the overall pass/fail determination using the four auto-passed results — thereby avoiding duplicate screening effort

all_rules.Rule_Name: Avoidance of Duplicate Screening Under 42 CFR 455.410
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Medicare Reciprocity feature is designed to comply with 42 CFR 455.410, which permits Medicaid agencies to rely on Medicare's provider screening results to avoid duplicating screening work already performed by Medicare/PECOS. This policy-based bypass has been inactive since 2014 as the enabling flag was never activated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been identified as UNSCREENED and is undergoing the screening process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The State License Verification check is performed against the state licensing board for the provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The license verification result must be recorded as PASS ('P') in the screening result indicator, confirming the provider holds a valid and active professional license

all_rules.Rule_Name: State License Verification Check Outcome Recording
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a provider undergoes state license verification, the system queries the state licensing board to confirm the provider holds a valid and active professional license, and records the outcome of that verification as a Pass result.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The state license verification check has been completed for a provider and the result is ready to be written to the screening output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the license verification output record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's NPI from the Provider Master Record must be copied into the screening output record's NPI field (SCR-NPI) to ensure the verification result is correctly attributed to the specific provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider NPI Captured for License Verification Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When recording the license verification result to the screening output, the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) must be captured from the Provider Master record and included in the screening output record to uniquely identify the provider associated with the verification result.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The license verification output record has been prepared with the provider's NPI and the verification result has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the license verification row to the Screen Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screening output record must have its check outcome status set to PASS (SCR-PASS = TRUE) and the complete record must be written to the Screen Output File (SCREEN-OUT-FILE), creating a traceable record of the license verification for the provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: License Verification Row Written with Pass Status to Screen Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the license verification result and provider NPI are captured, the screening output record must be flagged with a PASS status and written to the Screen Output File, creating a permanent audit record of the license verification outcome for the provider.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider has been identified as UNSCREENED and the overall provider screening process (SCREEN-ONE-PROVIDER) has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screening workflow reaches the license verification step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The State License Verification sub-process (CHECK-LICENSE) must be invoked to perform the license check, and upon completion must return control back to the main provider screening workflow to continue with the remaining checks (LEIE, SAM, DMF)

all_rules.Rule_Name: License Verification Invoked as Part of Provider Screening Workflow
all_rules.Rule_Description: State License Verification is a mandatory step that must be invoked for every unscreened provider during the provider screening process, unless Medicare/PECOS reciprocity is overriding the individual checks. The verification is triggered as a discrete sub-process within the overall provider screening workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record exists in the Provider Master File and is flagged as UNSCREENED
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider screening workflow is executed for that provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The OIG LEIE Exclusion Check must be invoked to query the Office of Inspector General's List of Excluded Individuals and Entities for the provider and all owners holding 5% or greater ownership interest

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke OIG LEIE Exclusion Check as Part of Provider Screening
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a provider is identified as unscreened, the OIG LEIE Exclusion Check must be invoked as a mandatory step in the provider screening workflow to verify the provider and their qualifying owners are not federally excluded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The OIG LEIE Exclusion Check has been executed for a provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The LEIE query completes and returns a result
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The LEIE verification result must be recorded as PASS ('P') for the provider, indicating the provider and their qualifying owners are not found on the OIG exclusion list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record OIG LEIE Verification Result for Provider
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the OIG LEIE Exclusion Check is performed, the verification outcome must be recorded against the provider so it can be used in the overall screening pass/fail determination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The LEIE verification result has been recorded for a provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the LEIE check result for writing to the screening output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's NPI must be captured from the Provider Master Record and the LEIE check outcome must be set to PASS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Provider NPI and Set LEIE Check Outcome for Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: Following the LEIE verification, the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) must be captured and the check outcome must be set to PASS so that a complete and identifiable screening result record can be prepared for output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The provider's NPI has been captured and the LEIE check outcome has been set to PASS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the LEIE verification result to the output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A row containing the provider's NPI and the LEIE check outcome of PASS must be written to the Screening Output File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write LEIE Check Result Row to Screening Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The LEIE check result, including the provider's NPI and the check outcome, must be written as a row to the Screening Output File to maintain a complete audit trail of all screening verifications performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The LEIE exclusion check result has been recorded for a provider along with the results of the License, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The overall screening outcome is determined for the provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the LEIE result is PASS along with all other three check results (License, SAM, DMF) also being PASS, the provider must be marked as SCREEN PASS; if the LEIE result is not PASS or any other check result is not PASS, the provider must be marked as SCREEN FAIL and the screening failure count must be incremented by 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: LEIE Result Must Pass for Provider to Achieve Overall Screening Pass
all_rules.Rule_Description: The LEIE exclusion check result is one of four mandatory checks that must all pass for a provider to be marked as an overall screening pass. A failing LEIE result alone is sufficient to mark the provider as a screening failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been identified as UNSCREENED in the Provider Master File and the SAM Debarment Check has been invoked as part of the screening process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SAM Debarment Check routine is executed for the provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system queries the System for Award Management (SAM) database to verify that the provider is not debarred or suspended from participating in federal programs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Query SAM Database to Verify Provider Debarment Status
all_rules.Rule_Description: When screening an unscreened provider, the system must query the System for Award Management (SAM) database to verify that the provider is not debarred or suspended from participating in federal programs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SAM Debarment Check routine has been invoked for an unscreened provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SAM database verification is completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The SAM verification result (WS-SAM-RESULT) is set to 'P' (Pass), indicating the provider is not debarred or suspended from federal programs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record SAM Debarment Verification Result as Pass
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon completion of the SAM debarment query, the system records the SAM verification result. In the current implementation, the SAM check result is recorded as Pass (P) for the provider being screened.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SAM debarment verification result has been determined for a provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screening output record for the SAM check
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's NPI (National Provider Identifier) is copied from the Provider Master Record into the Screen Output Record (SCR-NPI) to identify which provider the SAM verification result belongs to

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Provider NPI for SAM Debarment Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing the SAM debarment verification result to the screening output file, the system must capture the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) from the Provider Master Record and place it on the output record to ensure traceability of the screening result to the correct provider.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The provider's NPI has been captured on the Screen Output Record for the SAM debarment check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the SAM debarment output record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Screen Output Record status indicator (SCR-PASS) is set to TRUE (Pass), reflecting that the provider has passed the SAM debarment verification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark SAM Debarment Output Record as Pass
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screening output record for the SAM debarment check must be explicitly marked with a Pass status before being written to the Screen Output File, ensuring the output record accurately reflects the SAM verification outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Screen Output Record has been populated with the provider's NPI and the SAM debarment verification result status (Pass)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes preparation of the SAM debarment output record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A SAM debarment verification result row containing the provider's NPI and the Pass status is written to the Screen Output File (SCREEN-OUT-FILE), creating a permanent record of the SAM debarment check outcome for the provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write SAM Debarment Verification Result to Screen Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the SAM debarment verification result has been determined and the output record prepared with the provider's NPI and Pass status, the system must write a SAM debarment verification result row to the Screen Output File to maintain a complete audit trail of all screening checks performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has been identified as UNSCREENED and has been selected for screening, and the SSA Death Master File check step has been reached in the screening sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the SSA Death Master File check by querying the Social Security Administration Death Master File to verify that the provider is not deceased
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The DMF verification result is recorded as PASS (value 'P') in the DMF result field, indicating the provider is verified as not deceased in the SSA Death Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: SSA Death Master File Verification Result Recording
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the SSA Death Master File check is performed for an unscreened provider, the system queries the Social Security Administration Death Master File to verify the provider is not deceased and records the verification result as Pass.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SSA Death Master File check has been completed and a DMF verification result has been recorded for the provider
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screening output record for the DMF check result
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's NPI is copied from the Provider Master Record into the NPI field of the screening output record, ensuring the DMF result row is correctly associated with the provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider NPI Capture for DMF Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing the DMF check result to the screening output file, the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) must be captured from the Provider Master Record and placed into the screening output record to identify which provider the DMF result belongs to.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SSA Death Master File check result has been recorded as PASS and the provider's NPI has been captured into the screening output record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the DMF check result row to the Screening Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new record is written to the Screening Output File containing the provider's NPI and the DMF check result status set to PASS, creating a permanent audit trail of the SSA Death Master File verification for that provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: DMF Check Result Row Written to Screening Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the SSA Death Master File check is completed and the provider NPI is captured, a result row must be written to the Screening Output File recording the provider's NPI and the DMF check outcome as PASS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has completed all four compliance checks: State License Verification, OIG LEIE Exclusion Check, SAM Debarment Check, and SSA Death Master File Check, and all four results are recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screening verdict is being determined and the License result equals Pass AND the LEIE result equals Pass AND the SAM result equals Pass AND the DMF result equals Pass
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's record in the Provider Master File is updated with a status of SCREENING PASSED, indicating all compliance checks have been successfully cleared

all_rules.Rule_Name: All Four Compliance Checks Must Pass for Provider Screening Approval
all_rules.Rule_Description: A provider's overall screening verdict is determined by evaluating all four compliance check results together. Only when every single check — State License Verification, OIG LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File — returns a passing result is the provider granted a screening-passed status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider has completed all four compliance checks: State License Verification, OIG LEIE Exclusion Check, SAM Debarment Check, and SSA Death Master File Check, and all four results are recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screening verdict is being determined and at least one of the following is not a passing result: License Check result, LEIE Exclusion Check result, SAM Debarment Check result, or SSA Death Master File Check result
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's record in the Provider Master File is updated with a status of SCREENING FAILED, indicating one or more compliance checks were not cleared

all_rules.Rule_Name: Any Single Compliance Check Failure Results in Provider Screening Rejection
all_rules.Rule_Description: If any one or more of the four mandatory compliance checks — State License Verification, OIG LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, or SSA Death Master File — does not return a passing result, the provider is immediately marked as screening-failed, regardless of how many other checks passed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider has been evaluated for overall screening verdict and has been marked as SCREENING FAILED due to one or more compliance checks not returning a passing result
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screening failure status is recorded for that provider
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screening failure counter is incremented by exactly 1, accumulating the total number of providers who did not clear all compliance checks during this screening run

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screening Failure Counter Incremented for Each Failed Provider
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time a provider fails the overall screening verdict — meaning one or more of the four compliance checks did not pass — the program's running total of screening failures is increased by exactly one, enabling an accurate count of all failed providers to be reported at the end of the screening run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider's overall screening verdict has been determined as either SCREENING PASSED or SCREENING FAILED based on the four compliance check results
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screening verdict has been recorded on the provider's record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's updated record — containing the new screening status of either SCREENING PASSED or SCREENING FAILED — is written back and saved to the Provider Master File to permanently reflect the screening outcome

all_rules.Rule_Name: Provider Master Record Must Be Updated After Every Screening Verdict
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of whether a provider passes or fails the overall screening verdict, the provider's record in the Provider Master File must always be updated to persist the final screening outcome — either SCREENING PASSED or SCREENING FAILED — before processing the next provider.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider record has been evaluated through all four screening checks: License Check, LEIE Exclusion Check, SAM Debarment Check, and SSA Death Master File Check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All four screening check results — License Result, LEIE Result, SAM Result, and DMF Result — are each equal to 'Pass'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's screening verdict field in the Provider Master Record is set to SCREEN PASS, indicating the provider has successfully cleared all required screening checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Provider as Screening Passed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all four mandatory screening checks (License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File) return a passing result, the provider's screening verdict in the master record is updated to SCREEN PASS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider record has been evaluated through all four screening checks: License Check, LEIE Exclusion Check, SAM Debarment Check, and SSA Death Master File Check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: At least one of the four screening check results — License Result, LEIE Result, SAM Result, or DMF Result — is NOT equal to 'Pass'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's screening verdict field in the Provider Master Record is set to SCREEN FAIL, and the total screening failure count is incremented by 1, indicating the provider did not clear all required screening checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Provider as Screening Failed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When one or more of the four mandatory screening checks (License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, or SSA Death Master File) do not return a passing result, the provider's screening verdict is updated to SCREEN FAIL and the program-level failure counter is incremented.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider record has completed all required screening checks and the screening verdict (either SCREEN PASS or SCREEN FAIL) has been applied to the provider's master record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screening verdict determination is complete, regardless of whether the outcome is SCREEN PASS or SCREEN FAIL
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The updated provider master record — containing the new screening verdict — is rewritten back to the Provider Master File, permanently persisting the screening outcome for that provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: Persist Provider Screening Verdict to Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the screening verdict (PASS or FAIL) has been determined and applied to the provider record, the updated provider record must be written back to the Provider Master File to permanently record the screening outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A screening check (License, LEIE, SAM, or SSA DMF) has just been evaluated for a provider, and the provider's NPI exists on the Provider Master Record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to write a screening result row to the Screening Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The provider's NPI from the Provider Master Record is copied into the NPI field of the Screening Output Record, so that the result row is associated with the correct provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Provider NPI to Screening Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When writing a screening result row, the provider's National Provider Identifier (NPI) must be carried forward from the Provider Master Record into the Screening Output Record to ensure each result row is correctly identified by provider.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A screening check (License, LEIE, SAM, or SSA DMF) has been evaluated for a provider and the result has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to write the screening result row to the Screening Output File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The check outcome field on the Screening Output Record is set to PASS, capturing the result of that individual check prior to writing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Check Outcome on Screening Output Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing a screening result row, the outcome of the individual check (Pass) must be recorded on the Screening Output Record to reflect the result of that specific check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Screening Output Record has been populated with the provider's NPI and the check outcome for a specific screening check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the write operation for the screening result row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new result row is appended to the Screening Output File containing the provider NPI and the check outcome for that specific check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Screening Result Row to Screening Output File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the provider NPI and check outcome have been set on the Screening Output Record, a result row must be written to the Screening Output File. This occurs once for each individual check performed, resulting in one output row per check per provider.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unscreened provider is being processed through the full screening workflow
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Each of the four individual checks (License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, SSA DMF) is performed in sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A separate screening result row is written to the Screening Output File upon completion of each individual check, resulting in one row per check per provider

all_rules.Rule_Name: One Screening Output Row Written Per Individual Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screening output file receives one result row for each individual check performed — License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File — meaning up to four rows are written per provider during a full screening cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screening output row has been written to the Screening Output File as a result of the License check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to the License Verification step, allowing the screening workflow to proceed to the next check in sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to License Check After Writing Output Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the screening output row is written as part of the License check, control returns to the License Verification process so that the overall screening workflow can continue to the next check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screening output row has been written to the Screening Output File as a result of the LEIE Exclusion check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to the OIG LEIE Exclusion Check step, allowing the screening workflow to proceed to the next check in sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to LEIE Exclusion Check After Writing Output Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the screening output row is written as part of the LEIE Exclusion check, control returns to the OIG LEIE Exclusion Check process so that the overall screening workflow can continue to the next check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screening output row has been written to the Screening Output File as a result of the SAM Debarment check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to the SAM Debarment Check step, allowing the screening workflow to proceed to the next check in sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to SAM Debarment Check After Writing Output Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the screening output row is written as part of the SAM Debarment check, control returns to the SAM Debarment Check process so that the overall screening workflow can continue to the next check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screening output row has been written to the Screening Output File as a result of the SSA Death Master File check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to the SSA Death Master File Check step, allowing the screening workflow to proceed to the overall pass/fail determination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to SSA Death Master File Check After Writing Output Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the screening output row is written as part of the SSA Death Master File check, control returns to the SSA DMF Check process so that the overall screening workflow can continue to the final pass/fail determination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A provider has been evaluated through all applicable screening checks (License, LEIE Exclusion, SAM Debarment, and SSA Death Master File) and at least one of the four check results is not a Pass
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The provider is marked as SCREEN FAIL
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screening failure counter is incremented by 1, reflecting this provider as a failed screening case in the batch total

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screening Failure Count Accumulation
all_rules.Rule_Description: For every provider that does not pass all four screening checks, the system increments a running total of screening failures by one, accumulating the count across the entire batch run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All provider records in the Provider Master File have been read and evaluated for screening
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end of the Provider Master File is reached and the batch processing loop completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays a screening failure summary message identified with program name 'PRVSCR01', showing the label 'SCREENING FAILURES=' followed by the final accumulated count of providers who failed screening during the batch run

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screening Failure Summary Display at End of Batch
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all providers in the Provider Master File have been processed, the system displays the total number of providers who failed screening, providing an operational summary of the completed batch screening run.

description:
PRVSCR01 is a batch Screening and Verification Engine (PEM-2) that reads pending providers from the Provider Master File and performs eligibility screening by querying four external sources: the state license board, OIG LEIE (exclusion list), SAM (debarment registry), and SSA Death Master File. Based on the combined results, each provider record is updated with a pass or fail screening verdict, and a screening output record is written for audit purposes.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Indexed and Sequential Files) - **MQ Calls**: No (referenced in comments as real-world integration pattern, but no actual MQ CALL statements present in code) - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Provider Screening Initiation - Open the provider master file and screening output file to begin the batch screening and verification process for all pending providers 2: Pending Provider Selection - Read each provider record sequentially from the provider master file and identify only those providers with an 'unscreened' status for further processing 3: Medicare Reciprocity Check (Dead Code - Never Executed) - A feature intended to query PECOS (Medicare's enrollment system) to accept Medicare's prior screening results and automatically pass all four screening checks (license, LEIE, SAM, DMF), thereby avoiding duplicate screening work as allowed under 42 CFR 455.410. This feature has been inactive since 2014 because the enabling flag was never set to active 4: State License Verification - Query the state licensing board to verify that the provider holds a valid and active professional license, and record the verification result 5: OIG LEIE Exclusion Check - Query the Office of Inspector General's List of Excluded Individuals and Entities (LEIE) to verify that the provider and their owners (with 5% or greater ownership) are not excluded from federal healthcare programs, and record the verification result 6: SAM Debarment Check - Query the System for Award Management (SAM) to verify that the provider is not debarred or suspended from participating in federal programs, and record the verification result 7: SSA Death Master File Check - Query the Social Security Administration Death Master File (SSA-DMF) to verify that the provider is not deceased, and record the verification result 8: Screening Verdict Determination - Evaluate all four external screening results (license, LEIE, SAM, DMF) together; if all results pass, mark the provider as screening-passed; if any result fails, mark the provider as screening-failed and increment the failure counter 9: Provider Record Update - Write the updated screening verdict (pass or fail) back to the provider master file record 10: Screening Output Record Writing - Write a screening result row to the screening output file for each individual check performed, capturing the provider NPI and the check outcome 11: Screening Summary Reporting - After all providers are processed, display the total count of providers who failed screening to provide an operational summary of the batch run
